rules.title: No Dynamic Type
rules.check: The dynamic keyword is forbidden except for COM interop scenarios.
rules.rationale: Dynamic bypasses compile-time type checking. It hides bugs that would be caught by the compiler and reduces code maintainability.

rules.title: No Reflection for Business Logic
rules.check: Reflection must not be used for business logic. Reflection is permitted only for framework code.
rules.rationale: Reflection is slow, fragile, and difficult to maintain. Business logic must use compile-time safe patterns.

rules.title: No Thread.Sleep
rules.check: Thread.Sleep is forbidden. Task.Delay must be used for delays in async code.
rules.rationale: Thread.Sleep blocks the thread, wasting resources. It cannot be cancelled and does not work correctly in async contexts.

rules.title: No Empty Catch
rules.check: Empty catch blocks are forbidden. All exceptions must be logged or rethrown.
rules.rationale: Empty catches hide failures and make debugging impossible. Every exception must be recorded or propagated.

rules.title: No Catch Exception
rules.check: Catching base Exception is forbidden except at top-level handlers.
rules.rationale: Catching all exceptions masks specific failures. It catches fatal exceptions that should not be handled.

rules.title: No Mutable Statics
rules.check: Mutable static fields are forbidden except for thread-safe caches.
rules.rationale: Mutable statics create hidden state and race conditions. They make testing difficult and behavior unpredictable.

rules.title: No Service Locator
rules.check: Service locator pattern is forbidden. Dependency injection must be used.
rules.rationale: Service locator hides dependencies and complicates testing. Constructor injection makes dependencies explicit.

rules.title: No God Classes
rules.check: Classes exceeding 500 lines or 20 public members must be refactored.
rules.rationale: Large classes violate single responsibility. They are difficult to understand, test, and maintain.

rules.title: No Magic Strings
rules.check: String literals used as identifiers or configuration keys must be constants or nameof expressions.
rules.rationale: Magic strings break refactoring and enable typo bugs. Constants and nameof enable compile-time validation.

rules.title: No Obsolete API Usage
rules.check: APIs marked Obsolete must not be used in new code.
rules.rationale: Obsolete APIs will be removed in future versions. Using them creates technical debt and upgrade blockers.

rules.title: No GC.Collect
rules.check: Manual GC.Collect() calls are forbidden except in benchmarks or test cleanup.
rules.rationale: Manual GC disrupts the runtime's optimization. It causes performance issues and indicates design problems.

rules.title: No Direct Thread Creation
rules.check: Direct new Thread() is forbidden. Use Task.Run or thread pool.
rules.rationale: Manual threads bypass the thread pool and its optimizations. They make resource management difficult.

rules.title: No Ambient Context
rules.check: ThreadLocal<T> and AsyncLocal<T> for passing dependencies are forbidden. Use dependency injection.
rules.rationale: Ambient context hides dependencies and complicates testing. It creates implicit coupling that is hard to reason about.
